claim: Rreb1 is expressed within the embryo proper and extraembryonic supporting tissues.

claim: Rreb1 regulates neural tube closure.

claim: Rreb1 regulates cardiovascular development.

claim: At E4.5, Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the inner cell mass (ICM), comprising epiblast cells and primitive endoderm (PrE) cells, and the trophectoderm.
source: At pre-implantation stages (embryonic day (E) 4.5), Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the inner cell mass (ICM), comprising epiblast cells that will generate the fetus and primitive endoderm (PrE) cells that will give rise to the endoderm of the yolk sac, and the trophectoderm that will form the placenta (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At E5.5, before gastrulation, Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the PrE-derived visceral endoderm (VE) and trophectoderm-derived extraembryonic ectoderm (ExE), but not the epiblast.
source: In the early post-implantation embryo (E5.5), before gastrulation, Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the PrE-derived visceral endoderm (VE) and trophectoderm-derived extraembryonic ectoderm (ExE), but not the epiblast (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: During gastrulation (E6.5–7.5), Rreb1LacZ expression was observed within the VE, primitive streak, embryonic and extraembryonic mesoderm, and distal anterior epiblast.
source: Subsequently, during gastrulation (E6.5–7.5), expression was observed within the VE, primitive streak, a region where cells undergo an EMT and start to specify and pattern the mesoderm and endoderm germ layers, embryonic and extraembryonic mesoderm (derived from the primitive streak), and distal anterior epiblast (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Around midgestation (E8.0–10.5), Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the yolk sac endoderm, node, notochord, primitive streak, blood, allantois, head mesenchyme, and pharyngeal arches.
source: Around midgestation (E8.0–10.5), Rreb1LacZ was expressed within the yolk sac endoderm, node, notochord, primitive streak, blood, allantois, head mesenchyme, and pharyngeal arches (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–G.

claim: At E10.5, Rreb1LacZ was expressed in regions of high FGF signaling activity, including the limb buds, frontonasal processes, and isthmus.
source: We noted that at E10.5 Rreb1LacZ was expressed in regions of high FGF signaling activity (Morgani et al., 2018b), including the limb buds, frontonasal processes, and isthmus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and citation to Morgani et al., 2018b.

claim: The domain of Rreb1LacZ expression within the tailbud varied between embryos, suggesting that Rreb1 transcription may be regulated by the segmentation clock.
source: The domain of Rreb1LacZ expression within the tailbud varied between embryos, suggesting that Rreb1 transcription may be regulated by the segmentation clock (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by LacZ staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and inference from observed variability.

claim: Chimeric embryos containing Rreb1-/- ESCs showed that Rreb1-/- cells could undergo the gastrulation EMT, migrate within the wings of mesoderm, and differentiate into germ layer derivatives.

evidence: Supported by citation to Su et al., 2020.

claim: Rreb1-/- cells accumulated at the primitive streak over time in chimeric embryos, suggesting that later EMT events are perturbed.

evidence: Supported by citation to Su et al., 2020 and inference from observed accumulation.

claim: Rreb1+/- mice were viable and fertile.
source: Rreb1+/- mice were viable and fertile, but heterozygous intercrosses yielded no homozygous mutant offspring.
evidence: Supported by breeding data.

claim: From E7.5 onwards, Rreb1-/- mutant embryos were smaller than wild-type littermates.

evidence: Supported by brightfield images and quantification shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Based on morphology and somite number, Rreb1-/- embryos were approximately 9.5 hr retarded.

evidence: Supported by morphological analysis and somite counts shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: At E9.0–9.5, Rreb1-/- embryos showed microcephaly (2/7 at E9.5).

claim: At E9.0–9.5, Rreb1-/- embryos showed an open foregut.

claim: Some Rreb1-/- mutants close their neural tube upon further development.

claim: H2-Q2 regulates vasculogenesis and differentiation of blood lineages.
source: Loss of Rreb1 also led to increased expression of H2-Q2, a homolog of HLA-G that regulates VEGF expression through indirect mechanisms (Liu et al., 2020) as well as vasculogenesis and differentiation of blood lineages (Comiskey et al., 2003; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Comiskey et al., 2003 and Liu et al., 2020.

claim: The role of Rreb1 in vasculogenesis may be mediated via VEGF.
source: As Rreb1 functions downstream of, and regulates, receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, its role in vasculogenesis may be mediated via VEGF.
evidence: Speculative inference based on Rreb1's role in RTK signaling and VEGF pathway similarity.

claim: The yolk sac endoderm secretes factors that regulate cardiogenesis, vasculogenesis, and hematopoiesis.
source: The yolk sac endoderm secretes factors that regulate cardiogenesis, vasculogenesis, and hematopoiesis (Arai et al., 1997; Belaoussoff et al., 1998; Byrd et al., 2002; Damert et al., 2002; Dyer et al., 2001; Goldie et al., 2008; Miura and Wilt, 1969; Wilt, 1965).
evidence: Supported by citations to Arai et al., 1997; Belaoussoff et al., 1998; Byrd et al., 2002; Damert et al., 2002; Dyer et al., 2001; Goldie et al., 2008; Miura and Wilt, 1969; Wilt, 1965.

claim: The role of Rreb1 in embryonic vasculogenesis is likely mediated via paracrine interactions with the endoderm.
source: Thus, the role of Rreb1 in embryonic vasculogenesis is likely mediated via paracrine interactions with the endoderm.
evidence: Inferred from Rreb1 expression in yolk sac endoderm and downregulation of VE-secreted factors.

claim: In a cancer model, Rreb1 directly binds to the regulatory region of Snai1 in cooperation with TGF-β activated SMAD transcription factors to induce the expression of SNAIL, which drives EMT.
source: We previously showed that, in a cancer model, Rreb1 directly binds to the regulatory region of Snai1 in cooperation with TGF-β activated SMAD transcription factors to induce the expression of SNAIL, which drives EMT (Su et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Su et al., 2020.

claim: Both Rreb1-/- chimeric and mutant embryos did not show a total block to EMT, with cells able to exit the epiblast at the PS and differentiate into the embryonic germ layers.
source: Nevertheless, both Rreb1-/- chimeric (Su et al., 2020) and mutant embryos did not show a total block to EMT, with cells able to exit the epiblast at the PS and differentiate into the embryonic germ layers.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data showing germ layer differentiation and citation to Su et al., 2020.

claim: The Rreb1-/- phenotype is similar to that observed in Crumbs2 mutant embryos whereby the initial gastrulation EMT proceeds normally but over time, cells accumulate at the PS.
source: This phenotype is similar to that observed in Crumbs2 mutant embryos (Ramkumar et al., 2016) whereby the initial gastrulation EMT proceeds normally but over time, cells accumulate at the PS.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ramkumar et al., 2016 and inference from phenotypic similarity.

claim: Crumbs2 and Rreb1 are required for the later stages of gastrulation EMT.
source: This suggests temporally distinct EMT regulatory mechanisms in vivo with Crumbs2 and Rreb1 required for the later stages of this process.
evidence: Inferred from the similarity of Rreb1 and Crumbs2 phenotypes.

claim: In the mouse embryo, Rreb1 is expressed not only in mesenchymal tissues, such as the primitive streak and mesoderm, but also within epithelial tissues such as the trophectoderm, VE and the notochord.
source: Additionally, upon closer examination we found that loss of Rreb1 disrupts epithelial architecture. We found that, in the mouse embryo, Rreb1 is expressed not only in mesenchymal tissues, such as the primitive streak and mesoderm, but also within epithelial tissues such as the trophectoderm, VE and the notochord.
evidence: Supported by LacZ reporter expression data.

claim: Rreb1 does not drive EMT in all contexts.
source: Thus, Rreb1 does not drive EMT in all contexts.
evidence: Inferred from Rreb1 expression in epithelial tissues.

claim: In Drosophila, hnt exhibits context-dependent adhesion regulation.
source: Likewise, in Drosophila, hnt exhibits context-dependent adhesion regulation.
evidence: Supported by citations describing hnt function in different contexts.

claim: Loss of hnt in the trachea and retina disrupts epithelial architecture.
source: For example, loss of hnt in the trachea and retina disrupts epithelial architecture (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2000), while loss of hnt from border cells results in increased cell-cell adhesion (Melani et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pickup et al., 2002 and Wilk et al., 2000.

claim: Loss of hnt from border cells results in increased cell-cell adhesion.
source: For example, loss of hnt in the trachea and retina disrupts epithelial architecture (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2000), while loss of hnt from border cells results in increased cell-cell adhesion (Melani et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Melani et al., 2008.

claim: The function of Rreb1/hnt likely depends on the combination of factors and signaling activities present within any given cell where it is expressed.
source: Thus, its function likely depends on the combination of factors and signaling activities present within any given cell where it is expressed.
evidence: Inferred from context-dependent functions of Rreb1 and hnt.

claim: Rreb1 was shown to directly bind to the loci of a number of cytoskeleton regulators in HEK cell lines.
source: Rreb1 was also shown to directly bind to the loci of a number of cytoskeleton regulators in HEK cell lines (Kent et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kent et al., 2020.

claim: Hnt genetically interacts with and transcriptionally regulates cytoskeleton-associated genes, such as chickadee (Profilin1), karst (Alpha-actinin-1), jitterbug (Filamin A), dynamitin (Dynactin2), and Rho1.
source: Furthermore, Hnt genetically interacts with and transcriptionally regulates cytoskeleton-associated genes, such as chickadee (Profilin1), which governs actin polymerization and depolymerization, the F-ACTIN crosslinker karst (Alpha-actinin-1), Actin-binding protein jitterbug (Filamin A), a microtubule motor dynamitin (Dynactin2) and Rho1, a GTPase that regulates cytoskeleton organization (Oliva et al., 2015; Wilk et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Oliva et al., 2015 and Wilk et al., 2004.

claim: While the specific factors downstream of Rreb1 and hnt are distinct, these data suggest a conserved role in cytoskeleton regulation.
source: While the specific factors downstream of Rreb1 and hnt are distinct, these data suggest a conserved role in cytoskeleton regulation.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of Rreb1 and hnt targets.

claim: ACTIN interacts with cadherins and thus may directly influence their localization.
source: ACTIN interacts with cadherins (Han and de Rooij, 2017) and thus may directly influence their localization.
evidence: Supported by citation to Han and de Rooij, 2017 and inference from known interactions.

claim: The cytoskeleton mediates vesicular trafficking, which can also regulate E-CADHERIN localization.
source: The cytoskeleton mediates vesicular trafficking, which can also regulate E-CADHERIN localization (Aiello et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2003; Chung et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2015; Mary et al., 2002; Pilot et al., 2006; Sako-Kubota et al., 2014; Stehbens et al., 2006; Teng et al., 2005; Vasileva and Citi, 2018), and a large number of trafficking genes were upregulated in Rreb1-/- embryos.
evidence: Supported by citations to Aiello et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2003; Chung et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2015; Mary et al., 2002; Pilot et al., 2006; Sako-Kubota et al., 2014; Stehbens et al., 2006; Teng et al., 2005; Vasileva and Citi, 2018.

claim: A combination of altered vesicle trafficking and/or direct changes in the cytoskeleton may regulate E-CADHERIN localization in Rreb1-/- embryos.
source: Therefore, a combination of altered vesicle trafficking and/or direct changes in the cytoskeleton may regulate E-CADHERIN localization.
evidence: Inferred from the upregulation of trafficking genes and cytoskeleton changes.

claim: The epiblast phenotypes in Rreb1-/- could be due to a loss of low-level epiblast expression or an indirect effect of altered mechanical forces in the embryo stemming from perturbed EMT and, in mutant embryos, the VE.
source: As Rreb1 is not expressed highly within the epiblast, these phenotypes could be due to a loss of low-level epiblast expression or an indirect effect of altered mechanical forces in the embryo stemming from perturbed EMT and, in mutant embryos, the VE.
evidence: Speculative inference based on Rreb1 expression pattern and known mechanosensitivity.

claim: The expression of SNAIL and a number of other EMT and adhesion regulators is mechano-sensitive.
source: The expression of SNAIL and a number of other EMT and adhesion regulators is mechano-sensitive (Farge, 2003; Pukhlyakova et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2016), and thus changes in the physical forces within the embryo could underpin ectopic SNAIL expression within a fraction of epiblast cells.
evidence: Supported by citations to Farge, 2003; Pukhlyakova et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2016.

claim: Changes in the physical forces within the embryo could underpin ectopic SNAIL expression within a fraction of epiblast cells.
source: The expression of SNAIL and a number of other EMT and adhesion regulators is mechano-sensitive (Farge, 2003; Pukhlyakova et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2016), and thus changes in the physical forces within the embryo could underpin ectopic SNAIL expression within a fraction of epiblast cells.
evidence: Speculative inference based on mechanosensitivity of SNAIL expression.

claim: A reduction in ACTIN stress fibers enhances the motility and deformability of cells and is associated with an invasive phenotype in cancer.
source: A reduction in ACTIN stress fibers enhances the motility and deformability of cells and is associated with an invasive phenotype in cancer (Grady et al., 2016; Han et al., 2020; Katsantonis et al., 1994; Suresh, 2007; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Grady et al., 2016; Han et al., 2020; Katsantonis et al., 1994; Suresh, 2007; Xu et al., 2012.

claim: Altered ACTIN organization and punctate E-CADHERIN is indicative of an intermediate epithelial-mesenchymal state, which correlates with weaker cell-cell adhesion and collective invasion in metastasis.
source: Moreover, altered ACTIN organization (Gloushankova et al., 2017; Kovac et al., 2018) and punctate E-CADHERIN is indicative of an intermediate epithelial-mesenchymal state, which also correlates with weaker cell-cell adhesion and collective invasion in metastasis (Aiello et al., 2018; George et al., 2017; Jolly et al., 2015; Saitoh, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gloushankova et al., 2017; Kovac et al., 2018; Aiello et al., 2018; George et al., 2017; Jolly et al., 2015; Saitoh, 2018.

claim: Rreb1/hnt phenotypically interacts with and transcriptionally regulates ECM-associated factors such as viking (Col4a1), Cg25c (Col4a2), Mmp2, and Adamts5.
source: Rreb1/hnt phenotypically interacts with and transcriptionally regulates ECM-associated factors such as viking (Col4a1), Cg25c (Col4a2), Mmp2, and Adamts5 (Deady et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017; Wilk et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Deady et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017; Wilk et al., 2004.

claim: Changes in ECM composition in Rreb1-/- embryos may drive invasive behaviors.
source: Thus, changes in ECM composition in Rreb1-/- embryos may drive invasive behaviors.
evidence: Speculative inference based on ECM gene expression changes and observed invasive phenotypes.

claim: The complement and coagulation cascades control a variety of processes, including ECM remodeling, and the corruption of this pathway is linked to cancer metastasis.
source: Furthermore, KEGG pathway analysis of downregulated genes revealed that these were associated with the complement and coagulation cascades, which control a variety of processes, including ECM remodeling, and the corruption of this pathway is linked to cancer metastasis (Ajona et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ajona et al., 2019.

claim: ECM microtracks are bundles of parallel Collagen fibers observed in cancer.
source: These ECM tracks are reminiscent of bundles of parallel Collagen fibers, referred to as 'microtracks', observed in cancer.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of ECM microtracks in cancer.

claim: Microtracks are generated through ECM remodeling by invasive leader cells, which subsequently facilitates the migration of less invasive cells within the tumor.
source: Microtracks are generated through ECM remodeling by invasive leader cells, which subsequently facilitates the migration of less invasive cells within the tumor (Gaggioli, 2008; Gaggioli et al., 2007; Poltavets et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gaggioli, 2008; Gaggioli et al., 2007; Poltavets et al., 2018.

claim: Ectopic SOX2 + cells of wild-type origin were adjacent to Rreb1-/- cells.
source: Intriguingly, ectopic SOX2 + cells of wild-type origin were adjacent to Rreb1-/- cells.
evidence: Supported by confocal imaging data.

claim: Rreb1-/- cells might perform a role comparable to leader cells in cancer metastasis, remodeling the ECM to permit migration of wild-type neighbors.
source: Thus, Rreb1-/- cells might perform a role comparable to leader cells in cancer metastasis, remodeling the ECM to permit migration of wild-type neighbors.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the proximity of wild-type ectopic cells to Rreb1-/- cells and ECM remodeling.

claim: HLA-G (H2-Q2) upregulation is associated with metastasis and immune cell evasion.
source: HLA-G (H2-Q2) upregulation is also associated with metastasis and immune cell evasion (Liu et al., 2020) and, as a secreted factor, might also promote invasive behaviors in both wild-type and mutant cells.
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2020.

claim: As a secreted factor, H2-Q2 might promote invasive behaviors in both wild-type and mutant cells.
source: HLA-G (H2-Q2) upregulation is also associated with metastasis and immune cell evasion (Liu et al., 2020) and, as a secreted factor, might also promote invasive behaviors in both wild-type and mutant cells.
evidence: Speculative inference based on H2-Q2 upregulation and its secreted nature.

claim: The early mouse embryo is an experimentally tractable in vivo system to interrogate phenotypes related to epithelial integrity and invasion.
source: The early mouse embryo is an experimentally tractable in vivo system to interrogate these phenotypes and thus, future studies of the function of Rreb1 in development may also shed light on its role in metastasis and other diseases involving loss of epithelial integrity.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of the mouse embryo as a model system.

claim: Future studies of the function of Rreb1 in development may shed light on its role in metastasis and other diseases involving loss of epithelial integrity.
source: The early mouse embryo is an experimentally tractable in vivo system to interrogate these phenotypes and thus, future studies of the function of Rreb1 in development may also shed light on its role in metastasis and other diseases involving loss of epithelial integrity.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the similarity of developmental and disease phenotypes.
